verdictSummary:
Author-04 closes most of review-03 and the corrected root D9 direction:
- Owner-derived bounds and the byte law hold against my independently constructed owner maxima.
- D9 dominance, ties and cancellation match an independent reimplementation and the owner reference model's run selection, across all four formats.
- Closure is enforced in-process with a fresh-source loader; my PoCs confirm it.
- The coverage gap is isolated exactly.

Three findings remain:
- RPR4-1 (blocking): the page law still admits internally inconsistent sliced pages, where producedItems exceeds the embedded rows or totalItems. One is labelled complete-page-set.
- RPR4-2 (required): the D9 aggregate counts skipped required steps, which the pinned owner reference model excludes.
- RPR4-3 (required): RP-OBL-C01 is not tracked in the register, coverage or goldens.

requiredFindings.title: Page law does not join producedItems to totalItems or embedded rows; internally inconsistent sliced pages, including one labelled complete-page-set, are admitted
evidence: report_model.py:96-123 page_law relates producedItems only through `item_count > produced` and the cap test. There is no totalItems == producedItems join, and 'last page without cursor must embed every produced row' is implemented as `total != item_count`, not `produced != item_count`.

Owner laws:
- query-projection-contract.v3.md:136 (produced-item law: the prefix is producedItems; remaining units are owed and lower-bound)
- :140 (completeness = complete and exact)
- :146 (totalItems is qualified by countBasis; a produced prefix is never an unqualified total).
An exact complete answer produced exactly totalItems units, and a lower-bound totalItems is the produced prefix.

G4 (work/probes/probe_rpr4.json): audit-full slot 0 cut to 1 row. Context truncated-bound, lower-bound, producedItems = public cap 100000, totalItems forged to 1, no cursor. Result: accept. 99,999 produced rows are neither embedded nor continuable.
G5: visited cap reached, producedItems 50, totalItems 1, 1 row, no cursor. Result: accept.

G6: context complete, exact, totalItems 1, 1 row, producedItems 1000. Result: accept with continuation complete-page-set. This is the RPR3-1 class: a completeness label over a context that proves rows are missing.
Controls: G7 (complete with totalItems 107 but 1 row) gives J-GRAPH-COUNT; G8 (capped truncated-bound full page with valid cursor) is accepted.
Contract section 2 RPR3-1 and graph provenance 'owner-page-law-count-basis-coverage-produced-items-continuation' claim produced-item enforcement.
requiredFindings.correction: Add totalItems == producedItems for every graph page (exact: cardinality produced; lower-bound: produced prefix). Truncated-bound without a cursor then implies items == producedItems. Complete implies producedItems == items. Add G4-G6 as refusal cases with J-GRAPH-COUNT and rerun the byte-law scenario.

requiredFindings.title: The D9 aggregate counts skipped required steps; the pinned owner reference model excludes them

Owner reference model (pinned) docs/coop/design-corrections/workflows/workflows_model.v1.py:385-388 filters `r['outcome'] != 'skipped'` for classes, pick and matching. A skipped step is recorded with termination request-rejected REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED (:306), and all-skipped aggregates to success.

advisories.text: Closure alias bypass. Closure.governed compares normalised strings (check.py:61-65, 114-117). On the case-insensitive volume, PoC P9 read the unpinned docs/implementation/README.md through '/Users/sb/code/opensip-ai/OPENSIP_ARCH/...' under the hook without refusal, while the exact-case path is refused UNPINNED-LOAD. The traced checker never uses an alias, so this run's closure is sound, but 'refuses any unpinned open' is bypassable. Compare realpath plus (st_dev, st_ino) or case-folded paths.

check.py main calls tempfile.gettempdir() before the hook is installed, which writes and removes a probe file in TMPDIR (trace event 220 precedes the first pin read at 236). The summary field closure.declaredOutWrites reports 0 although --out was written, because the counter is serialised before the write.

The structural ledger bound is sound against schema maxima (slack 5,710 B per termination), but no owner record over 4 MiB passes the owner canonical codec (canonical.py MAX_BYTES; my maximal termination gives AdmissionError BYTE_LIMIT_OR_TYPE). If invocation:3 records are admitted through that codec, the reachable ledger is far smaller and the report admits ledger terminations no owner record can hold. Ask the workflow/identity owner to state the invocation record codec bound; RP-OBL-M01 must include the 27.8 MB case.

The static no-script section labels 'disclosure.historyPriorRunsInSnapshotHostAsserted' but 'disclosure.graphUnresolvedSubjects' carries no host-assertion marker, although descriptor-not-retained is hostAsserted in graph provenance. The document cannot prove host retention from untrusted JSON; browser admission (RP-OBL-B01) is shape, codec and internal joins only, and must not present verifiedInDocument labels as semantic proof.
The reportFeatures R05 row lists RP-DO-02 as keeping the row open until a successor, but the register marks RP-DO-02 conditional-not-selected, where the current state satisfies it.

The scoped coverage workaround value M1 matches the commands/version row. M0 also validates and M6 does not, so the proof is 'this key alone', not a derived milestone. The rationale is recorded; keep it outside historical bytes.

The register assigns obligations to other owners (native, security, workflow/invocation, query); these are proposals until those owners accept successors. RP-DO-11 (Attempt duration) implies an invocation successor and a ledger successor after M1 integration.
RP-DO-12 (explicit older Run selection, the review-03 A7 item) remains open; history is recent-only.
Generator integration was not run (RP-OBL-G01); the report and envelope5 const/allOf/oneOf constructs remain unexercised by the M1 generator.
